title: ambient does not work on minikube
body: I followed the ambient getting-started guide on minikube without installing Gateway APIs. I installed an Istio 1.19 development build with the ambient profile and an ingress gateway. The Bookinfo, istiod, ingress gateway, Istio CNI, and ztunnel pods all report Running and Ready, but the Istio CNI log reports `failed to get veth device: no routes found for 10.244.0.10`. It also contains missing-ipset and missing-iptables-chain warnings. This happens on minikube 1.30.1 on Fedora 38, while I do not see the error with KinD. I also recreated minikube with `--cni=kindnet`, but still got CNI errors.

symptoms_visible: On minikube, all of the ambient components and Bookinfo pods report Running and Ready, but the Istio CNI log says `failed to get veth device: no routes found for 10.244.0.10`.
The CNI log also contains missing-ipset and missing-iptables-chain warnings, and recreating minikube with kindnet still produces errors.
N0.label: N0 ambient CNI failure reported on minikube

symptoms_visible: With a newer development build and minikube's default auto CNI, the Istio CNI still reports `failed to get veth device: no routes found for 10.244.0.9`.
Running `ip route get` inside the CNI daemonset and its pod returns a route to the ztunnel address through `dev bridge`.
N1.label: N1 driver and raw route output collected

symptoms_visible: With minikube 1.31.1, the Docker driver, and kindnet, a request to Bookinfo returns HTTP 200 before I enable ambient on the namespace, but exits with code 7 after I add the ambient label.
The Istio CNI log now includes `failed to get ns name: failed to get namespace for 8`.
N2_x.label: N2_x Docker plus kindnet aftermath

symptoms_visible: When I try to install with `values.cni.cniNetnsDir=/var/run/docker/netns`, istioctl stops with `unknown field "cniNetnsDir" in v1alpha1.CNIConfig`.
I get the same validation error with the 1.20 and 1.21 development builds I downloaded.
N3_x.label: N3_x netns-directory flag unavailable in tested builds

symptoms_visible: I have not retested the final merged change on my own minikube cluster; another minikube tester reports that the latest build is working as expected.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available with third-party minikube confirmation

question_patterns: Which minikube driver are you using?
Can you share the minikube start command or the driver selected by your script?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using the kvm2 driver. My script defaults to kvm2, and I start the kindnet tests with `k8s-minikube.sh --cni kindnet start`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm using the Docker driver, not kvm2, and the node's network namespaces are already mounted into the CNI container.
I'm using qemu2 rather than kvm2, but otherwise use the same minikube script and CNI settings.

question_patterns: From inside the Istio CNI pod, what raw output do you get from `ip route get` using the CNI pod IP as the source and the ztunnel pod IP as the destination?
Please run a route lookup from the CNI daemonset container to the same-node ztunnel IP and paste the command and output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The CNI pod IP is `192.168.39.212` and the ztunnel pod IP is `10.244.0.9`. From both the daemonset and the pod, `ip route get from 192.168.39.212 10.244.0.9` prints `10.244.0.9 from 192.168.39.212 dev bridge uid 0`, followed by `cache`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The command returns `RTNETLINK answers: Network is unreachable` and prints no route to the ztunnel pod IP.
The same route is returned through `dev bridge`, but the CNI and ztunnel pod IPs differ from this run.

edges.comment: Issue comments c6-c9, reporter's minikube only: the reporter identifies kvm2 and performs the requested route measurement after recreating minikube with auto CNI and a newer development build. The answer preserves the raw `ip route get` output; interpreting `dev bridge` as incompatible with ambient's veth discovery remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Replace minikube's default networking and kvm2 combination with an explicitly supported-looking setup by starting minikube with the Docker driver and kindnet.
solution.concrete_example: Recreate the cluster with `minikube start --cni=kindnet --driver=docker`, reinstall the ambient profile, label the workload namespace, and retry the Bookinfo request.

edges.comment: Issue comments c10-c13, original reporter's system: participant1 recommended Docker plus kindnet, but the reporter's retained minikube 1.31.1 cluster still lost Bookinfo connectivity after ambient enrollment. This exact recommendation is therefore falsified as a complete fix, although it remains part of the eventual required configuration.

solution.intent: Use a nightly Istio build and configure the CNI network-namespace directory to the path used by Docker-backed minikube.
solution.concrete_example: With minikube using Docker and kindnet, install a nightly ambient build with `--set values.cni.cniNetnsDir=/var/run/docker/netns`.

edges.comment: Issue comments c14-c17, original reporter's system: the proposed value was not yet exposed through istioctl in either development build the reporter downloaded, so installation stopped at validation with an unknown-field error. The command made no persistent cluster change; S3 is retained.

solution.intent: Use an Istio build containing the completed minikube network-namespace support, run minikube with a veth-based CNI such as kindnet and a compatible driver, and configure the Docker network-namespace directory when that driver requires it.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to a current build containing the merged minikube CNI namespace support. Start minikube with kindnet and a supported driver such as Docker or qemu2; for Docker-backed minikube, install ambient with `values.cni.cniNetnsDir=/var/run/docker/netns`. Then enable ambient on a test namespace and verify workload connectivity before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers distinguish three observations: the early missing-ipset and iptables messages are cleanup warnings; the default minikube network exposes a bridge route rather than the veth topology ambient expected; and Docker-backed minikube requires Istio CNI access to its network-namespace directory. Mapping those observations to the completed minikube namespace-support change is engineer inference, not something the reporter stated.

edges.comment: Issue comments c17-c32, kept to the original minikube problem. The istioctl exposure and broader namespace-handling work were subsequently merged, and participant4 later reported that minikube worked as expected. That is a different affected operator's confirmation, explicitly folded as relayed evidence; the original reporter never confirmed the final build on their own system. Later Docker Desktop, telemetry, and mixed sidecar/ambient reports are separate problems and are excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted minikube compatibility problem: ambient requires a veth-based cluster CNI and access to the node's actual network-namespace directory; minikube's original CNI/driver defaults did not satisfy those requirements.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence, especially the CNI `failed to get veth device` error, the raw route through `dev bridge`, the driver information, and the Docker-plus-kindnet namespace lookup failure.

The fix must use an Istio build containing the completed minikube network-namespace support, with kindnet or another veth-based CNI and a compatible driver; Docker-backed minikube must use the Docker network-namespace directory where applicable.
Must not treat the initial missing-ipset or missing-iptables-chain cleanup warnings as the root cause.

Must not claim that switching only to Docker plus kindnet is sufficient, because that exact configuration still lost workload connectivity in the reporter's test before the namespace-directory support was available.

Must not treat the issue as verified by the original reporter until they retest workload connectivity on a build containing the fix; the thread only contains confirmation from a different minikube operator.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Kubernetes and Istio user who builds development versions, automates minikube startup, inspects daemonsets and pod YAML, runs commands inside CNI containers, and supplies complete logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and cooperative; pastes exact commands and raw output, repeats evidence when it was overlooked, and distinguishes personal impact from the value of documenting a reproducible platform requirement.
